SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which festival is held in Lamu? (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu Rain Day
   B. Nairobi Snow Day
   C. Lamu Cultural Festival
   D. Nakuru Fish Fair

2. How can a school show traditional culture? (1 mark)
   A. By holding a culture day with songs and dances
   B. By stopping all games
   C. By closing the library
   D. By locking classrooms

3. Who usually passes traditional culture on to children? (1 mark)
   A. Only shops
   B. Parents, grandparents and elders
   C. Only strangers
   D. Machines

4. Why is it important to check facts before telling your school's history? (1 mark)
   A. So that nobody listens
   B. So that the story is longer
   C. So that what you tell is true
   D. So that it is funny

5. What are school rules? (1 mark)
   A. Games
   B. Instructions on what we should and should not do
   C. Songs
   D. Lunch

6. What is a resource? (1 mark)
   A. A school rule
   B. A game
   C. A kind of weather
   D. Something we can use to meet our needs and earn a living

7. Which of these economic activities is a service? (1 mark)
   A. Teaching
   B. A crop of maize
   C. A stone
   D. A fish

8. What is an economic activity? (1 mark)
   A. A holiday
   B. A song
   C. Work done to earn income or make goods and services
   D. A game after school

9. Which item of clothing protects a worker's head in a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Skirt
   B. Sandals
   C. Helmet
   D. Scarf

10. What does jua kali mean in Kiswahili? (1 mark)
   A. Cold wind
   B. Big factory
   C. Hot sun
   D. Rainy day

11. Which is a service industry? (1 mark)
   A. A hotel
   B. A cement plant
   C. A sugar mill
   D. A dairy plant

12. Which of these helps drivers to see pupils on the road? (1 mark)
   A. A hat that covers the eyes
   B. A black bag
   C. Dark clothes
   D. Reflective strips

13. Which of these is a viable project? (1 mark)
   A. One that is dangerous
   B. One that costs more than it earns
   C. One that people want, is safe and can earn more than it costs
   D. One that nobody wants

14. What should be done with profit from a school project? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it away
   B. Hide it
   C. Agree together how to use it, for example to buy books
   D. Share it secretly

15. What does punctuality mean? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking loudly
   B. Running fast
   C. Arriving late
   D. Arriving on time

16. Which action shows cleanliness? (1 mark)
   A. Putting litter in the bin
   B. Throwing rubbish on the ground
   C. Writing on walls
   D. Spitting in class

17. Which is a benefit of good citizenship in school? (1 mark)
   A. More fights
   B. Less learning
   C. Property is broken
   D. The school is safe and orderly

18. What is a peace garden? (1 mark)
   A. A market
   B. A place for fighting
   C. A car park
   D. A garden where pupils can sit and be calm

19. What is a conflict? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. A book
   C. A disagreement or quarrel
   D. A holiday

20. Why is it important to plan a peace-building activity? (1 mark)
   A. So that it runs well and everyone knows what to do
   B. So that nobody joins
   C. So that it wastes time
   D. So that it is cancelled

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how tourism can benefit a county and its people. (5 marks)

22. State three things that spoil peace in school. (3 marks)

23. Give three reasons why economic activities are important. (3 marks)

24. Give three factors that promote peace in school. (3 marks)

25. Match each activity to a resource it uses: fishing, farming, mining, tourism. (4 marks)

26. Explain what jua kali workers do and why they are important. (4 marks)

27. Explain why some cultural practices are no longer kept. (3 marks)

28. Name the six aspects of traditional culture. (3 marks)

29. Explain what an industry is. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Lamu Cultural Festival
   The Lamu Cultural Festival celebrates coastal culture.

2. A — By holding a culture day with songs and dances
   A culture day lets pupils share their heritage.

3. B — Parents, grandparents and elders
   Culture is taught in families and communities.

4. C — So that what you tell is true
   History must be accurate.

5. B — Instructions on what we should and should not do
   Rules guide behaviour.

6. D — Something we can use to meet our needs and earn a living
   Resources include land, water, minerals and people's skills.

7. A — Teaching
   Teaching is work done to help others.

8. C — Work done to earn income or make goods and services
   Economic activities bring in income.

9. C — Helmet
   Helmets protect workers' heads.

10. C — Hot sun
   Jua kali means hot sun, from workers who work outdoors.

11. A — A hotel
   Hotels provide services.

12. D — Reflective strips
   Reflective strips shine in light.

13. C — One that people want, is safe and can earn more than it costs
   Viable means it can work.

14. C — Agree together how to use it, for example to buy books
   Profit should be used openly and wisely.

15. D — Arriving on time
   Punctual people arrive on time.

16. A — Putting litter in the bin
   Using bins keeps the school clean.

17. D — The school is safe and orderly
   Good citizens make a peaceful school.

18. D — A garden where pupils can sit and be calm
   A peace garden is calm and beautiful.

19. C — A disagreement or quarrel
   A conflict is a disagreement.

20. A — So that it runs well and everyone knows what to do
   Planning helps activities succeed.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: Visitors pay park and hotel fees. Guides and drivers get jobs. Hotels and shops earn money. Local crafts are sold. The county earns taxes to build roads and clinics.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bullying, fighting and spreading rumours. Accept stealing or discrimination.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: They provide food, they give jobs and income, and they earn taxes for county services.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Respect, sharing and forgiveness. Accept honesty, listening or fairness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each factor.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fishing uses lakes or ocean, farming uses land and soil, mining uses minerals, tourism uses wildlife or beaches.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: They make and repair goods such as furniture and metal doors in small workshops. They give jobs, provide cheap goods, and train young people in skills.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Some practices harm people, such as female genital mutilation and early marriage. The law forbids them. We keep the good parts and leave out the harmful ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for harm, 1 mark for law, 1 mark for keeping good parts.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports and games, and festivals and ceremonies.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, 1 mark for two or three.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: An industry is a place or business where raw materials are made into goods, or where a service is given to many people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for making goods, 1 mark for services or raw materials.
